**Finding: compliant** — no redline needed.

Paragraph 8(h) already reaches our fallback position and the substance of the preferred one for AP's side: AP may assign without Kubient's consent to an affiliate, to a purchaser of all or substantially all relevant assets, or to a successor by merger, stock sale or consolidation, and any other assignment requires consent that cannot be unreasonably withheld. Termination (paragraph 4(a)–(b)) is limited to convenience after the Initial Term, uncured material breach and insolvency — there is no change-of-control or deemed-assignment trigger and no Kubient right to terminate or re-price if AP is acquired, so no walk-away condition is engaged.

The only gap against the preferred position is symmetry: Kubient also enjoys the affiliate/successor carve-out, with no bar on assigning to an AP competitor. Given the otherwise balanced clause and AP's full M&A freedom, pushing for an asymmetric consent-plus-competitor-bar formulation would be disproportionate, so I have not proposed an edit.
